Maximize availability
Allows bookers to book meetings whenever a host is available. Use this to maximize the number of potential meetings booked and when the even distribution of meetings across hosts is less important.
Load balancing
We will monitor how many bookings have been made with each host and compare this with others, disabling some hosts that are too far ahead so bookings are evenly distributed.

Questions about round robin
How a host is picked, and what happens when plans change.
Ask a question
What's round-robin scheduling?
A team booking link that books one host per meeting. Bookers see every time any host is free, and each booking goes to the host whose turn it is.
How does Cal.com decide whose turn it is?
Among the hosts free at the time picked, priority comes first, then the host who was booked least recently. With weights on, the host furthest behind their share gets it.
How is it different from a collective event?
A collective event needs every host, so it only shows times they're all free. Round robin needs one host, so it shows every time anyone can take it.
What do weights do?
They give some hosts a bigger share of bookings. A host at 150% gets one and a half times the calls of a host at 100%, which helps when someone is new or part time.
What happens if a host can't make it?
The booking can be reassigned. Round robin picks the next free host, or you choose a specific team member, and the new host gets the booking with its details.
Can bookers keep the same host when they reschedule?
Yes. Turn on rescheduling with the same round-robin host, and a rescheduled booking stays with the host it had.
